name: Wikipedia Attention-Shock x Crowd-Loudness, Fear-Gated (genuine-attention onset, not price)
rationale: Two free, causal, un-revised crowd-attention signals quants ignore as 'social noise': Wikipedia page-view z-shocks (immutable counts, knowable T+1, never revised) and social loudness relative to dollar volume (social_excess_attention_z). Novel structure is a COMPOSITE distinguishing durable narrative ONSET from a crowded blow-off: require a fresh attention SHOCK (wiki z crosses UP through its own 30d baseline) WHILE the crowd is NOT already euphoric (fear_greed not greedy) and loudness-vs-money is elevated — the change-vs-altitude decomposition the registry already encodes (social_excess_attention_z continuation +1.8% t=+5.77; level leads DOWN). Hedge funds skip Wikipedia (no Bloomberg feed) and treat social as un-investable; an LLM-era pipeline reads it PIT-clean. DISCONFIRMER 1: replace the wiki z cross-up SHOCK with the raw wiki level via a fitted gt threshold — if a high-level threshold works equally, it is a drifting-level trap not a shock. DISCONFIRMER 2: drop the fear_greed gate — if the unconditional attention shock works the same, the 'not-yet-euphoric' composite adds nothing. DISCONFIRMER 3: substitute usgs_earthquake_count (a known non-causal noise control) for wiki views — if a noise series scores similarly the whole sweep is data-snooping.
catalyst: Narrative-onset attention surge: a fresh Wikipedia page-view z-spike for the asset's entity, confirmed by rising social loudness relative to dollars traded, while the broad crowd is not yet euphoric — clean attention onset that leads price before it is priced.
